title: Shopify development checklist for apparel brands that run weekly drops
primaryKeyword: Shopify store development for Indian brands
metaDescription: Shopify development checklist for apparel brands that run weekly drops: steps, mistakes to avoid and a 30-day plan from Altmash.
keywords: Shopify store development for Indian brands
intro: Most advice about Shopify store development for Indian brands is either too generic or written by people who have never had to hit a monthly target with it. I am Altmash, and everything in this guide comes from running live brands across fashion, ethnic wear, footwear, perfume and community platforms.
This guide is written for doers: clear steps, honest trade-offs, realistic budgets for Indian brands and a checklist you can hand to your team today.
takeaways: COD and trust signals matter for Indian buyers.
Product pages should answer every buying question.
Plan the catalog before uploading products.

sections.heading: What is really at stake with Shopify development
paragraphs: Shopify makes it easy to launch, but a store that sells consistently needs intentional structure: collections, product templates, filters and a checkout that feels safe to Indian buyers.
Your store setup also feeds your ads. Product titles, images, variants and the product feed decide how well Meta and Google catalog campaigns can perform.

The good news is that none of this needs a big team. It needs clear decisions, a weekly rhythm and someone who owns the result after launch — which is exactly how I run Shopify development for the brands I manage.

sections.heading: How much time and money Shopify development takes
paragraphs: A Shopify setup for an Indian brand typically ranges from about ₹25,000 for a theme-based build to ₹1,50,000 or more for custom design and integrations, plus monthly Shopify and app fees. Plan two to six weeks depending on catalog size.

These ranges are starting points, not quotes. The right number depends on your category, your margins and how much of the work your team can handle in-house. What matters most is committing to a test long enough to learn from it.

sections.heading: The 6-step framework I use
paragraphs: Here is the process I follow. The order matters: each step removes a reason for the next one to fail.
Give each step a clear owner and a deadline. A plan without owners is just a list of good intentions, and Shopify development punishes good intentions that never ship.
bullets: Plan the catalog: collections, tags, variants and naming rules before uploading products.
Choose a fast theme: prefer a lightweight theme and customise it rather than stacking apps.
Build strong product pages: clear photos, size guides, fabric or ingredient details, reviews and delivery information.
Set up payments and COD: an Indian payment gateway, COD rules and shipping zones.
Connect channels: Meta and Google feeds, pixels and analytics with correct events.
Optimise after launch: abandoned cart flows, one post-purchase upsell and monthly speed checks.

sections.heading: Selling to Indian and global buyers
paragraphs: In India, trust is often built in the chat window. A buyer who messages you on WhatsApp is judging your speed, tone and clarity as much as your product, so Shopify development has to include how your team responds.
Festive seasons, regional preferences and cash-on-delivery habits also shape results. Plan your calendar around them instead of treating every month the same.

sections.heading: The numbers that actually matter for Shopify development
paragraphs: Pick a small set of numbers and review them every week in the same place. I prefer five metrics the whole team understands over a dashboard nobody opens.
Look at trends over four to eight weeks rather than daily swings, and always tie the numbers back to revenue or qualified leads.
bullets: Store conversion rate and add-to-cart rate
Average order value
Return and RTO rate
Mobile page speed on product pages
Abandoned cart recovery rate

sections.heading: Your first 30 days
paragraphs: If you want to move quickly, here is how I would sequence the first month.
At the end of the month you will have real data instead of opinions — and a clear picture of where to invest next.
bullets: Week 1: Plan the catalog and choose a fast theme.
Week 2: Build strong product pages.
Week 3: Set up payments and COD and connect channels.
Week 4: Optimise after launch, then review your metrics and decide what to keep.

conclusion: If you take one thing from this guide, let it be this: Shopify development compounds when it is treated as a system. Fix the inputs, keep a simple scoreboard and give each change enough time to show results.

faq.q: Is Shopify good for Indian brands?
faq.a: Yes. Shopify supports Indian payment gateways, COD, shipping integrations and strong ad channel connections. It suits brands that want to launch fast and scale without managing servers.

faq.q: How can I reduce returns on my Shopify store?
faq.a: Add accurate size guides, real fabric or material details, multiple photos including on-body shots, and clear delivery and exchange policies. Most returns come from expectations not matching the product.

faq.q: How many apps should a Shopify store use?
faq.a: As few as possible. Each app can add scripts that slow the store. Keep apps for reviews, shipping and recovery, and remove anything that is not clearly paying for itself.

faq.q: Does Altmash work with brands outside India?
faq.a: Yes. Altmash works with Indian and international brands on branding, websites, Shopify, ads and full brand management, usually coordinated over WhatsApp and video calls.

faq.q: How does Shopify development connect with SEO?
faq.a: Clear structure, useful content and fast, focused pages help both search rankings and conversions. The same discipline that makes Shopify development perform usually makes your brand easier to find as well.
